flashcards.q: What's the fundamental difference between a React Server Component and traditional pre-RSC SSR?
flashcards.a: Traditional SSR ships the component's JS to the client to hydrate after rendering HTML. A Server Component's code never reaches the client at all -- it renders to a serialized RSC payload, and if it has no interactive behavior, zero of its JS is ever sent to the browser.

flashcards.q: Can a Client Component import and directly render a Server Component?
flashcards.a: No -- a Client Component's code runs in the browser with no server execution context to run the Server Component's async logic. The fix: a Server Component parent passes Server Components to a Client Component as children/props, treated as an opaque already-resolved slot.
A module boundary, not just one component -- everything imported into that file (transitively, unless it declares its own boundary) becomes part of the client bundle.

flashcards.q: How does streaming SSR with Suspense avoid the pre-RSC 'one slow query blocks the whole response' problem?
flashcards.a: The server sends the shell HTML and Suspense fallbacks immediately, then streams each boundary's real content independently as ITS OWN data resolves -- a slow section doesn't block a faster one from appearing as soon as it's ready.

flashcards.q: Why does <form action={serverActionFn}> work before JavaScript hydrates?
flashcards.a: Passing a 'use server' function directly as a form action makes it a genuine HTML form submission (a real POST with a serialized server function reference) -- native browser behavior requiring no client JS to have loaded.

flashcards.q: List three concrete causes of a hydration mismatch.
flashcards.a: 1) Browser-only APIs (window, localStorage) read unconditionally during server render. 2) Non-deterministic values (Date.now, Math.random, incrementing counters) used in initial render output instead of useId(). 3) Invalid HTML nesting silently restructured by the browser during parsing.

flashcards.q: What does React do when it detects a hydration mismatch?
flashcards.a: Discards the mismatched server-rendered DOM for the affected subtree and re-renders it entirely client-side -- causing visible flicker and potentially losing focus/form state, undermining SSR's benefit for that subtree.

flashcards.q: Why does useId() solve the generated-id hydration mismatch specifically?
flashcards.a: It derives a stable id from the component's position in the render tree rather than a random/incrementing runtime source, so server and client compute the SAME id for the SAME position deterministically.

flashcards.q: What changed about params/searchParams/cookies()/headers() in Next.js 16?
flashcards.a: They became strictly asynchronous -- must be awaited everywhere they're read. This is the highest-file-count breaking change in the 16 migration; a codemod handles most call sites automatically.

flashcards.q: What does Cache Components' 'use cache' directive do in Next.js 16, and how does it differ from the earlier caching model?
flashcards.a: Caches the function's rendered OUTPUT (not just raw data) with an auto-derived cache key, composing with Partial Prerendering for a static shell plus streamed dynamic parts. The earlier model's caching was largely implicit; Cache Components make it explicit and opt-in.

flashcards.q: Difference between revalidateTag() and updateTag() in Next.js 16?
flashcards.a: revalidateTag() is for content where eventual consistency is acceptable (a blog list that can lag by seconds). updateTag() is used in Server Actions when the acting user needs to see their own change immediately (a profile update).

flashcards.q: As of Next.js 16, what's the status of the App Router vs Pages Router?
flashcards.a: App Router is stable, primary, and recommended. Pages Router is explicitly in maintenance mode.

flashcards.q: Can a plain callback function be passed as a prop from a Server Component to a Client Component?
flashcards.a: No — a function is server-side code and code doesn't cross the RSC serialization boundary, only data does; passing one produces a runtime error. The one exception is a Server Action ('use server' function), which the framework serializes as an invokable reference, not literal function code.

flashcards.q: A Server Component renders a Client Component that needs an onClick handler. Where must that handler be authored?
flashcards.a: On the client side of the boundary, inside the Client Component itself — a Server Component can pass data props to a Client Component, but cannot author server-side and ship across an event-handling function as a prop, since functions don't serialize across the RSC payload.
